context.body: Selected for the reader trail because “Pilate questions; Barabbas is released; Jesus is handed over” preserves a distinct core source unit within sentencing.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Pilate, Jesus, chief priests, elders, the crowd, Barabbas, and Pilate’s wife each enter the sentencing scene.
observations.label: Pilate questions; Barabbas is released; Jesus is handed over: textual observation

observations.body: Questioning and silence give way to a release choice, a warning message, handwashing, crowd speech, flogging, and delivery.
observations.label: Pilate questions; Barabbas is released; Jesus is handed over: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: The governor’s seat, water for handwashing, and the prisoner exchange give physical form to the decision.
observations.label: Relationships named in Matthew 27:11–26

payload.posture: Read Matthew 27:11–26 as its own sentencing and mockery crucifixion setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: Pilate identifies Jesus as the one called Christ yet releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over after publicly distancing himself from the blood.
payload.title: Pilate questions; Barabbas is released; Jesus is handed over
